title: Full refund of order o_1001: button click to payment-provider refund
overview: The web app renders a Refund button carrying the order's display total (major units) in data-amount. The click is routed through the delegated data-action handler to requestRefund, which POSTs {order_id, amount} to the API's /refunds. The API routes by operationId from openapi.json to createRefund, which validates amount as an integer in minor units, stores a RefundRow, appends a refund.requested message to a JSONL topic file, and returns 202. The Python worker polls that topic, calls the payment provider with amount_minor=int(amount), and publishes refund.completed. The major/minor unit mismatch between web and API means a full refund becomes a 1/100 refund for whole-number totals and a 400 for totals with cents.

trigger.input: User opens the order page at ?order=o_1001 (seeded order: 49900 minor units SEK, status paid) and clicks the new 'Refund order' button

outcome: API answers 202 and the page shows 'refund requested'; the worker picks up refund.requested and asks the payment provider to refund amount_minor=499 (4.99 SEK, not the 499.00 SEK order total), then publishes refund.completed, which nothing consumes. The order and refund rows in the API stay 'paid' / 'requested'.

steps.summary: On load, the page reads ?order=o_1001, fetches the order and renders it into #app.
steps.details: Setup for the scenario: the button only exists after renderOrder runs. fetchOrder calls GET /orders/o_1001 (web/src/orders.ts:12).

steps.summary: GET /orders/{id} resolves to getOrder, which converts total_minor to major units via toPublic.
steps.details: Route comes from openapi.json operationId getOrder (api/openapi.json:7) mapped in handlers (api/src/handlers/index.ts:10). toPublic divides total_minor by 100, so the web receives total in major units, documented as such in api/openapi.json:19.

steps.summary: renderOrder now adds a Refund button with data-order-id and data-amount set from the order.
steps.details: Status is 'paid', so the button is rendered. data-amount is order.total, which is the major-unit display value from GET /orders.

uncertain.note: data-amount carries order.total in MAJOR units (499), but POST /refunds expects amount in MINOR units (api/openapi.json:43). Also the button only hides for status 'refunded'; nothing ever sets that status, so it reappears after reload.

steps.summary: The delegated click listener finds the closest [data-action] element and looks up actions['refund'].
steps.details:
Existing dispatch mechanism; the feature plugs in by adding a 'refund' key. Rejections are caught and rendered as a

steps.summary: The refund action disables the button and calls requestRefund with the order id and Number(data-amount).
steps.details: Reached by actions[el.dataset.action] at main.ts:9 and invoked at main.ts:11.

uncertain.note: On failure the button stays disabled forever and the status line is not updated; only an error paragraph is appended.

steps.summary: requestRefund POSTs {order_id, amount} to /refunds and types the reply as RefundRequested.
steps.details: Passes amount through unchanged; no conversion to minor units.

uncertain.note: This is where the unit conversion (x100, rounded) is missing; the API treats 499 as 499 öre.

steps.summary: post() sends JSON to BASE_URL + /refunds and throws on non-2xx.
steps.details: 202 is res.ok, so the JSON body is parsed and returned.

uncertain.note: A cross-origin POST with content-type application/json triggers a CORS preflight; the API has no OPTIONS route or Access-Control-* headers (api/src/server.ts:33-44), so this only works if web and API share an origin or a proxy sits in front. Not verifiable from these repos.

steps.summary: The HTTP server matches POST /refunds against the spec-derived routes and calls the handler with the parsed body.
steps.details: readBody JSON-parses the request; the handler's {status, body} is written back as JSON.

steps.summary: The new /refunds POST operation (operationId createRefund) defines amount as an integer in minor units.
steps.details: loadRoutes reads this spec at startup and builds a route per operation; the operationId names the handler.

uncertain.note: The spec is only used for routing; requestBody schema is not validated by the server, so the contract with web (which sends major units) is not enforced anywhere except by the handler's own checks.

steps.summary: createRefund is registered under its operationId so loadRoutes can find it.
steps.details: createRefund is registered under its operationId so loadRoutes can find it.

steps.summary: createRefund validates amount as a positive integer no larger than total_minor, stores a requested RefundRow, publishes refund.requested, and returns 202.
steps.details: o_1001 exists. amount 499 is an integer, > 0 and <= 49900, so it passes. The published payload uses the key amount (not amount_minor), with the same value stored in the row. Order status is never moved to 'refunded' and the RefundRow never leaves 'requested'; db is in-memory, so refunds are lost on API restart while the queue message persists.

uncertain.note: Validation accepts the web's major-unit 499 as 499 öre: a full refund silently becomes 4.99 SEK. An order with cents (e.g. total 499.5) would send 499.5 and get a 400. No check against previously requested refunds or order status, so repeated clicks (after reload) can over-refund.

steps.summary: publish appends one JSON line {topic, sent_at, payload} to QUEUE_DIR/refund.requested.jsonl.
steps.details: publish appends one JSON line {topic, sent_at, payload} to QUEUE_DIR/refund.requested.jsonl.

steps.summary: post() resolves with the 202 body and the action sets the .status text to 'refund requested'.
steps.details: The returned RefundRequested (refund_id) is discarded; the UI change is local only.

uncertain.note: UI says the refund is requested but nothing ever reports completion or failure back; a reload shows 'paid' and an enabled Refund button again.

steps.summary: The worker's poll loop iterates HANDLERS, now including 'refund.requested', and reads new messages for each topic.
steps.details: Linked to the API by the topic string 'refund.requested' (worker/worker/handlers/__init__.py:8) and the shared file naming QUEUE_DIR/<topic>.jsonl (worker/worker/queue.py:20 vs api/src/bus.ts:10). Both default QUEUE_DIR to /var/lib/shop/queue.

uncertain.note: A handler exception is logged and swallowed, and the offset still advances past the message (queue.py:29), so a failed refund (e.g. provider timeout) is never retried and nobody is told.

steps.summary: read() seeks to the stored offset, yields each new message's payload, then saves the new offset.
steps.details: read() seeks to the stored offset, yields each new message's payload, then saves the new offset.

uncertain.note: The offset is written only after all lines are consumed: if the worker dies after payments.refund succeeds but before line 29, the message is replayed and the customer is refunded twice (no idempotency key is sent to the provider).

steps.summary: handle_refund_requested passes order_id and amount_minor=int(payload['amount']) to payments.refund.
steps.details: handle_refund_requested passes order_id and amount_minor=int(payload['amount']) to payments.refund.

uncertain.note: Key mismatch is handled (API sends 'amount', worker reads 'amount'), but the value is already wrong by 100x from the web; int() would also silently truncate any fractional value.

steps.summary: refund() POSTs {order_id, amount_minor} to the provider's /v2/refunds and returns its refund_id.
steps.details: refund() POSTs {order_id, amount_minor} to the provider's /v2/refunds and returns its refund_id.

uncertain.note: Refunds 4.99 SEK on a 499.00 SEK order. Our refund_id is not sent, so the provider cannot dedupe retries or replays.

steps.summary: Logs the provider id and publishes refund.completed with refund_id, order_id and provider_refund_id.

steps.summary: Appends the refund.completed message to QUEUE_DIR/refund.completed.jsonl; this is the end of the trail.
steps.details: Appends the refund.completed message to QUEUE_DIR/refund.completed.jsonl; this is the end of the trail.

uncertain.note: No consumer of refund.completed exists in any of the three repos: the API never marks the RefundRow 'completed' or the order 'refunded', and there is no 'failed' path at all.
